angle_code_reality:
NO. `?a=` does not change the hero live today. Nothing on the funnel changes on the angle code.

I checked this directly. /LP, /LP?a=p&mk=au and /LP?a=m render word-for-word the same H1, subhead, bullets and images on mobile and desktop. The live page has no swap script. The angle table in LANDING_PAGE_COPY_SHORT §7 (m/s/j/p/t/run/r/n) and FUNNEL_PLAN §6 was never built. The plan itself says Funnelish native text slots can't read ?a=; the fix would be cloned pages (/match-m and so on) or ID'd text swaps, and neither exists.

What `a` actually does:
1. The native "Find my match" button forwards the whole query string. Clicking from /LP?a=p&mk=au landed on /quiz-2891028289-1791612140998314?a=p&mk=au. L1's passthrough script isn't needed for this, which is just as well because L1 isn't on the page. L1 only ever appended a/mk to custom quiz links; it never swapped the hero.
2. The quiz intro ignores `a`. It always reads "Let's find the pair you forget you're wearing."
3. QUIZ.html go() copies a and mk onto the offer-page URL.
4. OFFER.html url() copies a and mk onto the checkout URL.
No page renders anything differently from `a`. `mk=au` also does nothing, because L0 isn't live.

So `a` is only an attribution tag today. Every ad, whatever its angle, lands on the same hero: "Stop! I'll pee myself! / Common? Yes. Normal? No. / Find your match." Personalisation happens only inside the quiz, from her answers: Q1 moment, Q2 onset (persona card) and Q13 dream (offer headline). It does not come from the ad.
quiz_flow:
LIVE quiz: /quiz-2891028289-1791612140998314, which is QUIZ.html v3. I walked it end to end on 2026-10-13. It has 13 questions in 3 chapters, with cards in between.

INTRO
- Header: "Find your match"
- H1: "Let's find the pair you forget you're wearing."
- Sub: "A few quick questions about your moments. Then you'll see your size, how many pairs you need, and your free gifts."
- Button: [Start my match]
- Lines under it: "About 2 minutes · No email needed to see your match" and "This isn't a medical assessment. It matches you to underwear."
- The intro continues the landing's "Find your match" and its "size + how many pairs" promise.

CHAPTER "YOUR MOMENT"
- Q1 "When does it happen most?" Sneezing or coughing / Laughing / Jumping, running or the gym / All of these / Something else. This continues the landing's sneeze-laugh-jump bullet and the H1 moment. It is the ad-moment mirror.
- Card WHY: "Did you know. Why it catches you out. A sneeze, a laugh or a jump squeezes your bladder in a split second… It's pressure, not weakness. And that means it can be planned for." This is the not-her-fault beat.
- Q2 "When did it start?" After having a baby / In the last few years / When I started training more / As long as I can remember / Something else / I'd rather not say. This sets the persona.
- Card NORMAL (by persona). Every version ends "Common. Not normal. And you don't have to just live with it." This pays off the landing's "Common? Yes. Normal? No." The versions:
  - after a baby: "You're not the only one. About 1 in 3 women leak after having a baby.¹ Plumbing, not a verdict."
  - last few years: "It's not just you. Leaking gets more common as hormones change.¹"
  - training: "Strong women leak too. Studies put it at about 1 in 3 up to nearly half of women who do CrossFit.¹ It's pressure, not weakness."
  - other: Ridgeview "NEVER considered normal."
- Q3 (multi) "What have you tried?" Pads or liners / Period undies / Leak-proof undies / Pelvic floor exercises / Going to the toilet "just in case" / Crossing my legs / Something else / Nothing yet.
- Card REACT: "This is why nothing has worked" (or "Here's why most fixes don't stick"), up to 3 lines:
  - "Pads bunch and shift the second you move."
  - "Most undies aren't made for a sudden sneeze or jump."
  - "Crossing your legs works, until you laugh."
  - "Planning around toilets makes your day smaller."
  - "Exercises build strength slowly. Moments don't wait."
  - It closes with "It was never you. You needed something made for the moment, not more willpower."
  - This continues "Not a pad, not a diaper."

CHAPTER "WHAT'S HAPPENING"
- Q4 "How much leaks out?" (Be honest. It tells us if these will suit you.) A few drops / A small splash / More than a pad can hold / A lot. "A lot" triggers the HEAVY card: made for lighter leaks, see a doctor or pelvic floor PT, "See my match anyway".
- Q5 (multi) "Where does it happen?" At the shops / At the gym or on a run / With the kids / Out with friends / At work / At night / Somewhere else.
- Card PLAY: "That's [n] places you've been bracing for it. These moments come with no warning. Whatever you wear has to already be on when they hit. So let's make sure it's the right pair."
- Q6 "Have you bought things that promised to fix this?" No, first time / Once or twice / Lots of times / Yes, and I've given up. This is the burned-skeptic gauge.
- Q7 "What worries you most about leak-proof undies?" diaper feel / show under leggings / leak anyway / won't fit / thought leaking was normal / cost too much / something else. The answer is shown on the result.
- Q8 (multi) "What have you skipped because of it?" A class or a run / The trampoline with the kids / Light-colored pants / A big laugh / A long day out / Something else / Nothing yet.

CHAPTER "YOUR FIT"
- Q9 "When would you wear them?" Every day / On training days / At night / A mix.
- Q10 "What's your hip size?" S ≤36″ US 0–2 … 4XL 51–54″ US 20 / Over 54″. "Over 54″" triggers the NOSIZE card: "We'd rather tell you now… only goes up to 4XL."
- Card FIT: "And if the size is off? Email us within your 30 nights. We'll send your new size free. Nothing to send back."
- Q11 "What matters most?" That they hold / feel normal / don't move / last.
- Q12 "How often do you do washing?" Every few days / Once a week / Less than that.
- Q13 "What would you do first if you stopped worrying?" Jump on the trampoline with the kids / Go all out at the gym / Laugh as hard as I want / Wear whatever I want / Just stop thinking about it.

LOADER (about 7s): "Finding your match…" cycling "Matching your moments…", "Sizing you to this pair's chart…", "Working out how many pairs fit your week…", "Unlocking your free gifts…", "Your match is ready."

RESULT ("YOUR LEAK PROFILE / Here's your match. Built from your answers.")
- Tiles: Your moment (Q1), Your leak (Q4), Your week (Q9 + Q12), Your match "Size X · 5 or 10 pairs"
- "How much you leak" Light/Medium/Heavy bar with a "You" pin
- "Why this pair matches you": "Made for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump" · "Size X, matched to this pair's own chart" · "N pairs: enough …"
- "Your biggest worry": the Q7 answer, answered straight
- "Now / Next": photos for the Q8 and Q13 picks
- "Your free gifts are unlocked. Your N-pair set comes with a free Wash Bag ($12.95 value) / a free Wash Bag and free Wash Sheets ($32.90 in free gifts). And 30 nights to see if they hold."
- Button [See my offer], with "30-Night Leak-Test · Money back if they don't hold" under it

Set routing: wash "less than weekly" gives 10. Weekly wash plus every day, night or a mix gives 10. Everything else gives 5. 3 is never recommended.

promise_chain:
One message runs from first screen to checkout:

"Leaking on a laugh, sneeze or jump is common, but it isn't normal and it isn't your fault. There's black underwear that feels like underwear (not a pad, not a diaper). A 2-minute quiz works out your size and how many pairs you need. Then you test them on your own moment for 30 nights, and if they don't hold you get your money back."

How each step carries it:
1. AD must set up the moment (laugh / sneeze / jump) and ideally "common, not normal" and "not a pad".
2. LANDING: "Stop! I'll pee myself! / Common? Yes. Normal? No. / Find your match." + "Black briefs for women who'd rather laugh than cross their legs… size and how many pairs… 30 nights to see if they hold" + "Feels like underwear. Not a pad, not a diaper." + "Built for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump" → [Find my match].
3. QUIZ INTRO: "Let's find the pair you forget you're wearing" + "your size, how many pairs you need, and your free gifts".
4. Q1 replays her moment, then the WHY card ("pressure, not weakness").
5. Q2 sets the persona, then the NORMAL card ("Common. Not normal. And you don't have to just live with it.") with a matching stat.
6. Q3 asks what she's tried, then REACT ("Pads bunch… It was never you").
7. Q4–Q8: honesty filter, places, burned-ness, worry, what she's skipped.
8. Q9–Q12 set fit and count. The Fit Promise card sits in here.
9. Q13 asks for her dream.
10. RESULT: "Here's your match", "Made for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump", her worry answered, "Your free gifts are unlocked", "30 nights to see if they hold" → [See my offer].
11. OFFER: "Your N pairs are ready, size X. Next stop: [dream]." Set pre-selected, gifts unlocked, "Sneeze in them. Laugh in them. Then decide." Pads vs Leapproof.
12. CHECKOUT: "Free shipping · 30-Night Leak-Test · Free size swap", "Matched to your quiz answers."

The three words carried from start to end are MOMENT, MATCH and 30-NIGHT TEST. Price, set sizes and gifts only appear after the quiz. Age, postpartum, perimenopause and training only appear inside the quiz (Q2, Q5, Q8, Q13 and the NORMAL card), never on the landing page.

angles_supported.quiz_continuation: Q1 'When does it happen most?' (Sneezing or coughing / Laughing / Jumping, running or the gym), then the WHY card 'A sneeze, a laugh or a jump… It's pressure, not weakness.' Q8 'A big laugh' and Q13 'Laugh as hard as I want' carry through to the offer dream line 'Next stop: laughing as hard as you want.'

I'll pee myself!') and the landing repeats it word for word. A LAUGH moment is the best match because the H1 is a laugh line. Sneeze is next best (bullet, quiz Q1, offer 'Sneeze in them'). And you don't have to just live with it.', with a sourced stat or the Ridgeview quote 'NEVER considered normal.' Q7 option 'I thought leaking was just normal' is answered on the result: 'Common, yes. Normal, no. You don't have to just live with it.'

Q11 'That they feel normal'. Offer table: 'Like your regular undies'. Intro: 'the pair you forget you're wearing.'

angles_supported.angle: Not a pad, not a diaper (pads & liners bunch, feel like a diaper, go in the bin)

angles_that_break.why: Meta personal-attributes rule and the FUNNEL_PLAN §6 'you' test. The landing also never mentions age or life stage, so the hero won't echo it.

angles_that_break.angle: Clinical / condition-led: incontinence, bladder weakness, SUI, 'protection', 'discreet', 'accident', doctor or PT-recommended, 'fix / cure / stop leaks', 'Kegels don't work'
angles_that_break.why: Banned words and fake-authority. The landing (when complete) says 'Not a treatment. It's underwear.' The quiz says it's not a medical assessment. Nothing hands off.

angles_that_break.angle: Overnight / heavy leaks / 'can't make it to the bathroom' / 'stay dry all day'
angles_that_break.why: The product is for light leaks. Quiz Q4 'A lot' sends her to a 'may not be enough' card. The landing is all laugh, sneeze and jump. 'Dry' or 'holds' as a claim isn't supported by a founder test.

angles_that_break.angle: Smell / embarrassment / 'nobody will know' shame hooks
angles_that_break.why: Never-shame rule plus the banned 'discreet' frame. The landing has no smell or hiding message (its joke is laughing, not hiding).

angles_that_break.angle: France 1985 / 'America hands you a pad' advertorial
angles_that_break.why: The planned `n` body copy and the France fact aren't on the live landing. A story-led ad would arrive at a 3-line hero plus reviews, with nothing to continue the story.

cj_claim_limits:
Every ad must respect these limits. Sources: FUNNEL_PLAN §2/§6/§8.1, NUMBER_SHEET §1–5/§11/§13, BRAND_BIBLE §12–13, LANDING_PAGE_COPY_SHORT §9.

1. Enemy sentence, exact CJ wording only: "Pads and liners bunch, feel like a diaper, and go in the bin every day." Never attack period underwear or period pads. Never say "built for pee, not blood" or "period products can't handle urine".

2. No mechanism.
- No Leak-Lock, no pour or spill demo, no absorbency (ml or oz), no "lab-tested".
- No layer count; say "layered" at most.
- No "sealed edges" or "wicking core".
- Only checkable facts are allowed: a soft, stretchy black brief with a leak-resistant lining from front to back, wider at the back, washable, reusable.

3. No absolute performance claims.
- Never: "leak-proof" as a claim, "100%", "zero leaks", "never leak", "stays dry", "stops leaks", "holds" as a claim.
- Allowed: "leak-resistant", and only once the in-house wear test is logged (LANDING flag 1 BLOCKER).
- Allowed: "made for lighter leaks", and only if the sample passes the founder test.
- "Hold" may appear only inside the guarantee condition: "see if they hold" / "if they don't hold".

4. Banned words in ads: incontinence, SUI, bladder weakness, protection, dignity, discreet, accident, medical-grade, clinically proven, doctor or gynecologist recommended, cure, fix, treat, prevent UTIs, non-toxic, PFAS-free. Say "manage", never "fix".

5. Meta "you" rule. No second-person statement about her condition, age, postpartum or menopause status ("you leak", "your bladder", "after your baby", "your perimenopause", "Do you suffer from…"). Use a first-person moment ("I'll pee myself"), third person, the moment itself, or the product.

6. Open on the moment (sneeze, laugh, jump, run, trampoline). Never lead with shame, smell, hiding or fear.

7. No fake proof.
- No invented reviews, testimonials, ratings, review counts or UGC presented as customers. FTC 16 CFR 465 applies, and the brand has 0 customers.
- No fake doctors or experts, no fake founder, no countdowns, no fake scarcity, no "most popular", no "compare at" anchors.
- Any creator content must be a real person with disclosure ("Received a free set to test" / "Paid partner").
- AI-generated people must not be presented as real customers.

8. Stats and quotes: only NUMBER_SHEET §11 exact text with the source.
- "About 1 in 3 women leak after having a baby." (PMC8295150)
- CrossFit always as the range "about 1 in 3 up to nearly half". Never "1 in 5".
- "Leaking becomes more common with age". Never "half by 50s" to a 40s audience.
- Ridgeview: Leaking is "NEVER considered normal." (word for word)
- No "endorsed by" framing.

9. Guarantee and Fit Promise: locked wording only.
- "30-Night Leak-Test" / "Wear them through your moment for 30 nights. If they don't hold, you get your money back." (+ "You keep the pairs.")
- Terms: from delivery, one claim per customer.
- Never "risk-free", "free trial" or "lifetime".
- Fit Promise: "Wrong size? We'll send your new size free. Nothing to send back."

10. Product facts.
- Plain black brief, no lace.
- Fabric is 95% regenerated fiber / 5% spandex. NOT "cotton".
- Sizes S–4XL, hips up to 54″ (about a US 20).
- Black only.
- Free shipping on every set, "about 6–10 days" (ships from overseas).

11. Numbers come only from NUMBER_SHEET (USD).
- Sets: 3/$45, 5/$59, 10/$99.
- Gifts: Wash Bag on 5 ($12.95 value); Wash Bag + Wash Sheets on 10 ($32.90). No gifts on 3.
- Gift values only while the gifts are genuinely listed at those prices in Shopify.
- For the first top-of-funnel campaign, keep prices out of the ads.

12. No competitor names (Everdries, Knix, Thinx and so on). Attack the pattern, not a brand.

13. Every ad must hand off to the one live hero: "Stop! I'll pee myself! / Common? Yes. Normal? No. / Find your match." The CTA should be the quiz ("Find my match" / "2-minute quiz").
live_issues: FABRICATED REVIEWS LIVE on the landing (high risk). Three named, rated 'customer' reviews show while the brand has zero customers: 'Jess M. Rate 4.6', 'Sarah Williams Rate 4.8', 'Jessica Miller Rate 4.9'. They carry customer-style claims ('Two weeks in…', 'Stayed dry and nobody knew a thing', 'The XL fits like my normal undies') and a UGC-style photo of briefs and a mailer bag on a bed. This breaks the FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR 465), Meta deceptive-practices policy, the CLAUDE.md non-negotiables and the locked build, which calls for STRAIGHT ANSWER cards with no name, photo or stars. The reviews also make unsupported performance claims ('stayed dry'), use a 'nobody knew' (discreet) frame, and use AU slang ('nan', 'undies', 'supermarket') in a US-first funnel. Remove them before any traffic.

Everything below the hero is missing. L0 top bar, the 3 Straight Answer cards, the L1 strip (Ridgeview proof, 3 steps, second CTA), the L2 footer and the L3 sticky bar are not on the page. The live page ends after the review carousel. As a result:
- (a) 'Money back if they don't hold' is advertised with NO terms on the landing: no #leak-test block, no 'from delivery', no 'one claim per customer'. FTC 16 CFR 239 guarantee disclosure is not met.
- (b) 'Common? Yes. Normal? No.' has no source on the page.
- (c) No 'Not a treatment. It's underwear.' and no quiz disclaimer.
- (d) No Privacy, Terms, Refunds, Shipping or Contact links, no business identity and no US limited-warranty text. Meta ad review and payment processors expect these.
- (e) No AI-image disclosure. The paste list says 'The image at the top is AI-generated. It doesn't show real customers.' The carousel's four women in briefs read as real people or customers.

Mobile CTA is below the fold. At 390x844 the 'Find my match' button sits at about y 860–905, so the first screen ends on the bullets. It is lower still in the Instagram and Facebook in-app browsers. The mobile chip 'LEAK-RESISTANT UNDERWEAR', the under-button micro-copy 'About 2 minutes · No email needed to see your match' and the sticky bar are all absent. The carousel autoplays every 5s, while the plan says autoplay off. The first capture had already rotated to the back-view slide.

?a= angle codes do nothing. The hero is identical for every code. No swap code or /match-[code] clones exist, and the quiz intro is static. `a` is passed through to quiz, then offer, then checkout as an attribution tag only. mk=au does nothing because L0 isn't live. Every angle must fit the one laugh hero, or angle pages must be built before the ads run.

No Meta pixel on any funnel page. fbq and ttq are undefined on the landing, quiz, offer and checkout; only Funnelish analytics and Stripe load. Cold Meta conversion campaigns can't optimise for InitiateCheckout or Purchase. The offer page's fbq('track','InitiateCheckout') silently does nothing.

Health data goes into URLs, which must be fixed BEFORE the pixel is added. The quiz sends answers to the offer page in the query string, for example ?size=XL&set=10&p=c&o=n&k=h&w=t&r=s.c.p.2.s.0.n.c.e.XL.h.w.t&a=m. Here p=c means 'after having a baby', and r holds every answer, including leak amount and what she's tried. This contradicts FUNNEL_PLAN §7 ('never put health answers in URLs'). The offer page only reads size, set and w, so p, o, k and r carry risk with no benefit. Once a Meta pixel loads, PageView would send them to Meta: Meta's health-data restrictions apply, and the plan itself flags US consumer health data privacy. Drop those params or use sessionStorage or an opaque code.

Funnel runs on leapproof.myfunnelish.com. try.leapproof.com/match and /LP both return 404, so the branded domain isn't connected yet. NUMBER_SHEET §12b says never put the Funnelish subdomain in ads. It's a trust hit for the roughly one third of buyers who've been burned. The old misspelt leepproof.myfunnelish.com also 404s, so the correct spelling is the one live.

Template metadata left in place. The browser tab title is 'Landing Page' on the landing, quiz and offer pages. There's no meta description, no OG title, description or image, and no planned 'Find Your Match | leapproof' title or /match slug. In-app browsers show 'Landing Page' in the header, and shared links preview blank.
